text:
Front incisor root pin broke  (after previous repair at local hospital) and now an implant was the only viable course of action.   After visiting several places, I settle on Dr. Nan  (his nickname).   Besides being license here, he attended a year of implant training at UCLA (California USA) and has good mastery of the English language.  He was prepared to explain everything in writing and was most willing to answer questions without pressure or rushing you.

During the many visits, he took great care to reduce discomfort and to verify his work.  Because this was a very visible area of the mouth he made  a temporary bridge from flow-able resin.  No one could tell I was having work done.

Please understand he certainly isn't the cheapest place around, but as with most things, you get what you pay for.   What impressed me also was "no surprises" of up-charging for extras.

Dr. Nan has training from several of the major implant makers.  In my case we decided on a mid range implant made by Anyridge.  This was after much web investigation and consultation.   I won't know for sure until years down the road if I made the correct decisions of doctor and device; but I am pretty sure I did.
